content.text: As Matt Zumwalt suggests, this issue should also be considered for the reworking of the REST API and therefore possibly included in 3.3
The REST API seems to be supporting Content-Length correctly (and for HEAD) - can we close this?

I could be wrong, but I don't think the REST interface sets Content-Length for Managed Content datastreams. I tested with exactly the same datastream content in Fedora 3.4, and only the inline XML version set Content-Length.
I'm not sure if this is desired behaviour or not, but it seems inconsistent. Examples below.
On the Content-Range side of things, Fedora seems to ignore Range headers for both managed and inline datastreams:
It'd be super awesome if it could return these headers properly.
I can confirm that the content-length header is NOT being set when Fedora 3.4 serves managed datastreams:
Here's the output of the request and response headers:
== Info: About to connect() to localhost port 8080
== Info: Server auth using Basic with user 'fedoraAdmin'
== Info: About to connect() to localhost port 8080
== Info: Server auth using Basic with user 'fedoraAdmin'

In the absence of a "Content-Length" header being set by the servlet, Tomcat sets a "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" header on the response.  This causes problems in some HTTP/1.1 applications, such as the Quicktime plugin for Firefox in Mac and Windows.

Hi Scott - we also noticed the discontinuity you pointed out between the old-style API-A and the REST interface in relation to Content-Length a couple of days ago, so thanks for posting this useful information on it.

"In the absence of a "Content-Length" header being set by the servlet, Tomcat sets a "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" header on the response. This causes problems in some HTTP/1.1 applications, such as the Quicktime plugin for Firefox in Mac and Windows. "

I can corroborate the strange behaviour in the QuickTime plugin (among other applications) when using the REST-style URLs with media files. I hadn't noticed the 'chunked' header, but that seems to explain it.

I've been looking at the code that seems to set the Content-Length headers for API-A getDatastream(Dissemination) and will contribute a patch for REST if I can put together some code. Anyone else who has ideas/code on this front, please get in touch with me
We're on the verge of deploying Fedora for HTML5 media streaming so we can also give any improvements that need tested a thorough check.

Datastream size is now available for new managed content datastreams (but not existing ones - overdue is a migration utility to calculate and persist size for these) - so theoretically it should be possible to provide this header.  I didn't manage to spot anywhere in the code where this is being added to the headers from a quick look through though.

There's something relevant around line 658 to 675 of FedoraAccessServlet.java in trunk. I'm not sure how the 'dissemination' object is structured but it seems to be a this point that the MIME type is added to the response headers, so perhaps Content-Length could go in there too,

FedoraAccessServlet looks like it might be a good place to calculate and set the Content-Length header... but I'm wondering if it would be worthwhile to set it down lower, as a field in MIMETypedStream?  Then the size wouild be available globally.  Do you have an opinion on this, Steve?

Not set the header itself in MIMETypedStream, of course... but calculate the size, set a field, and create a method to retrieve it from MIMETypedStream objects.  Then it could be accessed any place where a MIMETypedStream is used, such as in FedoraAccessServlet.
Persistence of size for managed datastreams addressed by
Existing managed content datastreams (prior to 3.4) won't have the size attribute calculated (
addresses calculation of size for those

The size for managed content datastreams is preserved as a datastream (version) attribute in the FOXML.  The size is calculated in DefaultDOManager.doCommit, see lines 1210, 1215, 1218.  The ILowLevelStorage interface was modified in 3.4 to return the stream's size on addDatastream and replaceDatastream (this is supported by Akubra, but potentially may not be supported by external ILowLevelStorage implementations).

It sounds reasonable to me to use MIMETypedStream to carry this information.  MIMETypedStream currently has a "header" field (org.fcrepo.storage.types.Property[]).  The header field is currently set for example to return a content-disposition header indicating the filename to be used for a datastream; and the BaseRestResource.buildResponse returns the contents of this header field (and others, potentially including content-length) as HTTP headers.  So it would seem the route to go down if MIMETypedStream could consistently be populated with the appropriate content-length header.

Probably need to think about what to do for external content, whether we persist the size in the FOXML, when to update this size (for instance, a HEAD request to the external content and inspection of last-modified/etags to determine if the size is "current") - I think there were some discussions about this at a committer's meeting.
Thanks, Steve.  I'll work on setting a Property "Content-Length" header for MIMETypedStreams.

On the Content-Range side of things, Fedora seems to ignore Range headers for both managed and inline datastreams:

curl -u myuser:mypass -I -r 0-40 http://myrepo:8080/fedora/objects/gcu:134/datastreams/testinline/content

It'd be super awesome if it could return these headers properly.
